column13: Isolate from only 1 patient. CLSI broth microdilution
column14: A 57-year-old male received a stem cell transplant in may 2012 and received fluconazole daily since then as a prophylaxis. One month later, in July 2012, the patient was admitted for pulmonary invasive aspergillosis. The patient agreed to participate in a double-blinded phase III clinical trial comparing two azoles with anti-Aspergillus activity. However, the clinical condition of the patient deteriorated rapidly even with azole therapy. The isolate showed an azole-resistant phenotype, with high resistance to voriconazole (MIC>16 mg/L) and resistance to itraconazole (MIC =4 mg/L) and posaconazole (MIC =1 mg/L). Because of that, the investigators decided to withdraw the patient from the clinical study. Nine days after the start of azole therapy, liposomal amphotericin B was started at a dose of 3 mg/kg. Nevertheless, the patient developed widespread IA with eye and brain involvement. The patient died 19 days after admission for IA. Azole resistance in the strain affecting the patient was shown to be due to cyp51A mutation TR46/Y121F/T289A.
